mia: Heads-up — our token-level SLO panels in ap-southeast-1 are showing a cost/latency regression at p99 after ~18:00 UTC. p99 jumped ~2.6x, tokens/sec dropped on a few shards. digging. :magnifying_glass_tilted_left:
ashok: saw that alert from `sre-bot`? can you paste the panel or promql?
lucas: alert-bot posted: "ALERT token_p99_high (ap-southeast-1): token_p99 > 350ms for 5m". link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abcd/token-slo?orgId=1
mia: putting key graphs here: p50/p95/p99, TTFT, tokens/sec histogram, and per-shard hotness heatmap. main promql for p99 is `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, region, shard))`
emily: can we confirm whether this is GPU contention (hot shard) vs network egress serialization? last week a similar blip was NVLink saturating on a host.
lucas: quick drill I ran: `sum by (instance) (rate(gpu_utilization[2m]))` — some instances at 99% while others are 20%. looks like uneven routing.
nashok: also check `inference_requests_tokens_total{region="ap-southeast-1"}` vs `requests_served_by_shard` — if tokens/sec per shard drops but total queue grows, autoscaler didn't react.
mia: pasted a small snippet from pod logs where a server started logging slow KV cache misses: ```[2026-02-21T18:05:12Z] WARN cache.go:142 miss batch fetch time=24.8ms shard=hot-3 model=gpt-3x-q4
[2026-02-21T18:05:12Z] INFO rpc.go:87 served tokens=512 latency=412ms
```
emily: that latency line looks like TTFT (time-to-first-token) not full completion. SLO is 99th TTFT for token streams.
lucas: suggestion: add a Grafana panel split by `quantization` and `cache_hit` labels so we can see if q4 models + cache_miss are the combo causing spike. also create a recording rule: `record: instance:token_p99:5m` to avoid heavy query load.
nashok: agree. also we should tune the alert: right now it fires on p99 > 350ms across region; noisy when single-hot-shard spikes. change to: fire when p99 > 350ms AND tokens/sec > 5000 (region) for 10m OR when >=3 shards have p99 > 350ms. reduces single-shard noise.
mia: can someone update the runbook with steps? quick checklist: 1) check `kubectl get pods -n inference -l shard=hot-* -o wide`; 2) check GPU host metrics `nvlink, rx_tx, iops`; 3) check cache miss rates and prefix cache evictions; 4) if hotshard, rebalance routing weight or scale dedicated pool.
nashok: I'll add the alert change as a PR to infra-alerts repo and add the recording rule.
lucas: for probing repro, run a targeted load test to the hot shard: `python perf/load_shard.py --region ap-southeast-1 --shard hot-3 --duration 5m --qps 1200` — that should exercise batching dynamics.
emily: cost note: observed token cost per 1k tokens in ap-southeast-1 rose by ~18% during the window due to fallback to larger model variant during capacity pressure. need to check routing policy fallbacks.
mia: good call — check `routing_policy_fallbacks_total{from_model="gpt-3x-q4",to_model="gpt-3x-fp16"}` for the window.
sre-bot: [Alert] token_p99_high cleared for ap-southeast-1 (duration: 22m).
deploy-bot: recorded deploy events: `canary routing-policy v2.4` at 2026-02-21T17:58:03Z (user: ops/rollouts).\ashok: that deploy might explain the sudden reroute; it changed `regional_weight` heuristics for hot shards. I opened https://git.internal/infra/PR/289 to revert if needed.
mia: action items: (1) ashok + lucas: add recording rule + update alert -> PR today; (2) emily: run cost impact calc and share numbers; (3) lucas: run targeted load and capture histograms + nvlink metrics; (4) mia: update runbook with step-by-step and add checklist for fallback rollback.
emily: sharing quick cost calc in channel later. initial estimate: extra $0.9k for the 6h blip (provisioning + model fallback).
lucas: once PRs merged, we should add a Grafana panel that shows `tokens/sec` vs `token_cost_per_1k` aligned by time so we can correlate cost spike with fallback events.
mia: thanks all. leaving follow-ups in the PRs and I'll create a `postmortem-lite` if cost > $1k. :white_check_mark:
